title: Jadumani Singh Wins Silver in Men's 55kg Boxing at CWG 2026
excerpt: The 22-year-old Manipur boxer won four unanimous 5-0 bouts before falling to Australia's Jye Dixon in the final, capping India's dominant boxing campaign in Glasgow with 10 medals.
body:
• Jadumani Singh Mandengbam won silver in men's 55kg boxing at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, losing the final 0-5 to Australia's Jye Dixon on August 1.
  • The 22-year-old from Manipur swept through four rounds with perfect 5-0 unanimous decisions before the gold medal bout.
  • India's boxing contingent claimed 10 medals in Glasgow — seven gold and three silver — making it the country's most successful sport at CWG 2026.
  • Jadumani's silver adds to his growing international resume after a silver and bronze at the 2025 World Boxing Cup.

Dixon Dominates the Final

India's Jadumani Singh Mandengbam fell short of gold in the men's 55kg boxing final at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, losing 0-5 to Australia's Jye Dixon at the SEC Centre in Glasgow on August 1. All five judges scored the bout in the Australian's favour, ending what had been a flawless run for the young Indian pugilist through the tournament, according to Wikipedia's official results page.

https://x.com/PiyushGoyal/status/2083577138201182546

Dixon, who had also been impressive throughout the competition, proved too strong on the night, using his reach and timing to deny Jadumani the top step of the podium. The silver medal, however, marks a significant achievement for the 22-year-old, who had entered the Games as a rising prospect rather than a frontline favourite.

A Dominant Path to the Final

Jadumani's road to the gold medal bout was nothing short of spectacular. He opened his campaign with a commanding 5-0 unanimous decision over Scotland's Aaron Cullen in the Round of 32, controlling the bout from start to finish with all five judges scoring every round 10-9 in his favour, according to IANS.

His Round of 16 clash against Pakistan's Sumama Rehman on July 26 carried extra significance — it fell on Kargil Vijay Diwas. Jadumani delivered another 5-0 sweep, with three judges scoring the bout 30-27 and two returning 29-28 verdicts. Despite Rehman's height and reach advantage, the Indian's footwork and sharp combinations proved decisive.

"I dedicate my win to the Kargil heroes... I felt great winning against Pakistan. I will perform even better in the quarterfinals."

— Jadumani Singh, after his Round of 16 victory (via ANI)

He continued his dominance with another 5-0 win over Zambia's Mwengo Mwale in the quarterfinals on July 28, and dispatched Namibia's Philip Haoseb by the same margin in the semifinals on July 31. Four bouts, four unanimous decisions — 20 out of 20 judges backing him before the final.

From Football Dreams to Boxing Ring

Born on May 5, 2004, in Iroishemba near Imphal, Manipur, Jadumani initially dreamt of becoming a footballer before his uncle introduced him to boxing, according to Inshorts. He competed in the 50kg weight class through much of his early career, winning silver at the World Boxing Cup Finals in Noida and bronze at the World Boxing Cup in Foz do Iguaçu, both in 2025.

The move to 55kg this season proved transformative. As MyKhel reported from Glasgow, Jadumani had often struggled to make the 50kg weight limit, shedding significant weight before bouts. The shift to 55kg allowed him to carry more natural weight into the ring, and he compensated for any height disadvantage with superior technique and ring intelligence. At just 22, his best years in the sport lie ahead.

India's Boxing Juggernaut

Jadumani's silver was part of a historic boxing haul for India in Glasgow. The contingent of 14 boxers — seven men and seven women — claimed 10 medals: seven gold and three silver, making boxing India's most successful sport at CWG 2026, according to The Sporting News.

The gold medallists included Sachin Siwach (60kg), Ankush Panghal (80kg), Preeti Panwar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg), Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg). Fellow silver medallists were Lovlina Borgohain (75kg) and Narender Berwal (+90kg). India finished the Games with 39 medals overall — 13 gold, 17 silver, and 9 bronze — placing fourth in the medal table.

What the Silver Means for the Diaspora

For the Indian community in Scotland and across the UK, the boxing events at the SEC Centre became a rallying point throughout the Games. Jadumani's emotional dedication of his Round of 16 victory to Kargil war heroes on July 26 resonated with Indian fans worldwide, blending sporting excellence with national sentiment. His silver medal adds to Manipur's growing reputation as a boxing powerhouse, following in the tradition of Mary Kom and Lovlina Borgohain.

What's Next

Jadumani's transition to the 55kg category — which aligns with Olympic weight classes — positions him as a serious contender for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. His Glasgow showing, where he was clearly the second-best boxer in his division across the Commonwealth, gives him a strong platform to build on. With World Boxing recognising the 55kg category at the Olympic level, the young Manipuri fighter's best chapters may still be unwritten.
nri_angle: Jadumani's emotional Kargil dedication resonated with Indian fans in Glasgow and across the UK, while his silver adds to Manipur's boxing legacy following Mary Kom and Lovlina Borgohain.
